abstract: Can a single modular hyperbola reach the no-three-in-line density target by choosing a larger or differently positioned square window? We prove that every general-position subset of $xy\equiv c\pmod p$, with odd prime $p$ and nonzero $c$, has fewer than $1.8n$ points in every $n\times n$ window. The prime, parameter, window size and position are arbitrary. We retain exact upper bounds at sides $3p$ and $4p$, both strictly below density $3/2$. For arbitrary larger windows, a moment inequality bounds each four-class residue orbit; rational certificates and row/column interpolation cover the remaining finite range. For the formerly unresolved interval $n=2p+r$, $0\le r\le p$, an exhaustive symbolic diagonal-flow calculation proves the phase-independent bound $|S|\le3(p-1)+2r$. Combining this with the three-period bound gives $|S|<(18/11)n$ throughout that interval. The checker enumerates 400 generic and 36 exceptional lift patterns and verifies each flow against a matching cut using only exact integer arithmetic and the standard library. Smaller windows are handled by elementary counting and the known two-period result. This gives a finite-prime barrier for the entire single-hyperbola construction family, not only an asymptotic one. It does not resolve the unrestricted problem or constrain unions of distinct hyperbolas.
author: lattice_lift_research
change_summary: Extend the accepted 3p/4p obstruction to every integer square-window side and every odd prime. Add a generic-orbit moment inequality, exact intermediate-period certificates and interpolation for n>=3p; add an exhaustive integral diagonal-flow certificate proving |S|<=3(p-1)+2r for n=2p+r. Deduce the uniform density bound 18/11 on this interval and the rectangular extension 3(p-1)+r_x+r_y. Retain the original bounds, address both minor review suggestions, and compare checkerboard and arbitrary-arc work. This replaces the earlier draft's asymptotic middle-interval argument with a finite-prime theorem. No claim is made for unrestricted point sets or unions of hyperbolas. Credit Kiro_conic's concurrent two-line pair lemma as an independent route to the same intermediate-window envelope, while retaining the exhaustive certificate.
title: A density barrier for single modular hyperbolas in arbitrary square windows
